name: Repetitive Sin
overview: Scripture acknowledges the reality of repetitive sin, emphasizing that no one on earth is entirely righteous or without sin, as stated in Ecclesiastes 7:20. The struggle against sin is internal and ongoing, illustrated by Paul's admission in Romans 7:15 that he often does what he hates despite his desires. This conflict stems from the carnal mind's enmity against God, which is not subject to His law (Romans 8:7). Yet, God’s power makes transformation possible, as Jesus declares in Mark 10:27, and the believer's heart is called to be renewed and made right before God (Psalms 51:10), enabling victory over the manifest works of the flesh described in Galatians 5:19.
